themes_detail.label: Mysterious SPIT Spike
themes_detail.summary: Special Projects Inspection Team complaints surged to 5 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.4 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 1,233% spike (z-score 9.55)—suggesting either a concentrated enforcement action, a new code violation hotspot, or a data reporting anomaly worth investigating.
evidence: 5 SPIT complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1,233% increase, z-score 9.55)
SPIT is DOB's specialized enforcement unit; spike is statistically extreme and warrants clarification
No prior signals in constituent cases or local news, suggesting this may be newly detected
reporting_angles: Contact DOB to understand what triggered the sudden increase in SPIT activity—is there a code enforcement crackdown underway?
Identify which buildings or block faces are the focus; interview affected property owners

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints from parks jumped to 16 LAST WEEK, a 374% increase over the 8-week baseline of 3.4 per week (z-score 4.0), indicating either a new noise source, increased park use, or special events.
evidence: 16 park noise complaints LAST WEEK vs. 3.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (374% increase, z-score 4.0)
Community board has requested new/expanded park amenities, but noise surge suggests existing parks may lack adequate management
Timing suggests possible seasonal trend (weather improving) or a specific event triggering complaints
reporting_angles: Identify which parks are generating the complaints and what noise sources residents are reporting (construction, events, late-night gatherings)
Interview Parks Dept and community board about park management capacity and enforcement of hours/noise regulations

themes_detail.label: Bus Stop Shelter Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Bus stop shelter complaints exploded to 3 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 0.2 per week (1,100% spike, z-score 4.16), suggesting rapid deterioration or inadequate maintenance of transit infrastructure in Bushwick.
evidence: 3 bus stop shelter complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1,100% increase, z-score 4.16)
This week's spike is the most extreme after SPIT; suggests acute deterioration or damage
Converges with community board requests for new/expanded transit amenities, indicating ongoing transit infrastructure neglect
reporting_angles: Map the specific bus stops with complaints; photograph conditions and compare to other NYC neighborhoods
Interview MTA and 311 to understand what 'shelter complaint' codes capture—broken glass, graffiti, structural damage, cleanliness?

themes_detail.label: Sanitation Crisis Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary condition complaints nearly doubled to 78 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 36.5 per week (114% increase, z-score 4.0), and dirty condition complaints remain chronically high at 518 over 90 days—indicating a sustained sanitation failure aligned with community board requests for DSNY capital spending.
evidence: 78 unsanitary condition complaints LAST WEEK vs. 36.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (114% increase, z-score 4.0)
Dirty condition complaints persist at 518 total over 90 days—one of top 3 complaint categories alongside noise and parking
Community board has filed repeated annual requests for DSNY capital spending, indicating chronic, unresolved problem
reporting_angles: Interview residents on which blocks or areas are worst affected; document visual conditions with photos/video
Request DSNY data on collection frequency, staffing levels, and recent changes in service routes in CD 304
Investigate whether the sanitation spike correlates with any staffing changes, budget cuts, or special events

themes_detail.label: Tree Die-Off Pattern
themes_detail.summary: Dead/dying tree complaints spiked to 4 TWO WEEKS AGO from a baseline of 0.8 per week (433% increase, z-score 4.91), suggesting either climate stress, pest damage, or a concentrated problem area worth ground-truthing.
evidence: 4 dead/dying tree complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (433% increase, z-score 4.91)
Converges with community board's repeated requests for green infrastructure and stormwater management projects
Timing suggests possible seasonal pattern (spring awakening revealing winter damage) rather than acute event
reporting_angles: Locate the specific trees reported and assess whether complaints cluster geographically or along particular streets
Interview NYC Parks about pest management, watering protocols, and plans to replace dead trees in the district
